language.script_notes: Greek alphabet with letters such as Σ, λ, Ω, Δ and Ψ; road signs are usually bilingual with a Latin transliteration beneath the Greek. Place names use endings like -άτα (common on Kefalonia) and -ανά or -ές (common on Crete and in the mountains). Telephone area codes begin with 2, such as 21 (Athens), 231 (Thessaloniki), 266 (Corfu) and 28 (Crete).

road_furniture.bollard_color: Bollards with a red reflector on a black background.
road_furniture.line_paint: Almost all main roads have median strips with double white center lines, a very characteristic Greek look.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Chevrons show white arrows on a black background (as in Albania). Telephone poles are often made of wood. Warning signs often have an orange background (also seen in Poland and North Macedonia), while speed-limit signs are on a white background, unlike North Macedonia's orange. Small chapel-like roadside shrines called kandylakia mark memorials.

architecture.roof_style: Reddish-brown tile roofs on mainland houses; flat roofs on remote islands.
architecture.roof_material: Red-brown clay tile on the mainland.
architecture.wall_construction: White-plastered walls with reddish-brown roofs are the classic look; flat-roofed, whitewashed cubic houses on the Cycladic islands; concrete-frame apartment blocks in Athens and other cities.
architecture.wall_color_palette: White walls with blue trim and doors, and reddish-brown tile.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Whitewashed churches with blue domes; roadside shrines (kandylakia); ancient temples and ruins; small island villages of stacked white houses (Hydra has no cars at all, and Sifnos has more than 300 churches).

nature.vegetation: Olive groves everywhere, vineyards throughout, cotton fields on the flatlands, pine and scrub on dry hillsides, and bare white limestone karst rock showing through in many areas.
nature.terrain: A mountainous mainland and thousands of islands, with rugged coastlines, dry hillsides and limestone karst; flat plains only in the north and center.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, dry, sun-bleached Mediterranean summers with bright light and a deep blue sea on the horizon.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text and, since 2004, a blue strip on the left with the EU stars and 'GR'.
vehicles.plate_format: Three letters, a hyphen and four digits from 1000 (e.g. 'ΑΒΓ-1234'); Athens and Thessaloniki are marked by just the first letter and other districts by the first two.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Taxi colours vary by city — yellow in Athens, silver in Heraklion and dark blue in Thessaloniki; scooters and small trucks.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage of the mainland and the larger islands; some small islands are thin.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Neighbouring Balkan landscapes, similar chevrons (Albania) and orange warning signs (North Macedonia)
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Greek alphabet, double-white center lines and white speed-limit signs distinguish this country.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Aegean coast, olive groves, similar landscape and apartment blocks across the sea
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Greek script and churches versus Turkish Latin script with ı and ş and mosques; Greek plates have three letters and four digits.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Mediterranean architecture, olive groves and terracotta roofs
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Cyprus drives on the left and uses British-style signs; Italy uses red-diagonal bollards and 'Via' street names, while Greek script appears here.
